unit: gzip bytes, KB = 1000 bytes. Every growth, share and identity rule compares the hash-normalized sizes of the report, the key normalized, measured with the content hash of every emitted file name replaced by a fixed placeholder, and cap applies to the raw size as built. growth is the cumulative allowance over the 0.3.0 baseline after each 0.4.0 stage (null: no growth limit), the share of a stage is its growth minus the growth of the stage before and bounds the growth over the stage base, a row whose share in a stage is 0 must equal the stage base in that stage, cap is a fixed limit in bytes (null: a growth-only row), and exact keeps a row identical to the baseline while its growth is not null

frozen.why: Stages 1 and 4 add no code to the browser paths, stage 3 adds only its 0.01 KB share to the ISO BMFF parser and stage 6 adds code only to the rule entries. These stages keep every row that no group gates identical to the report they start from, and every stage keeps every gated row whose share in the stage is 0 identical to it. Every row that holds the ISO BMFF parser is gated with the ISO BMFF share for each copy of the parser it holds, so the stage 3 parser change moves only gated rows, each within its share. The listed rows are the only other rows such a stage may move: the critical path, the entry chunk and the check chunk of the check and preset configurations in stage 6.

files.why: A sum row such as firstMp4, allOwn or lazyTotal adds up whole files, so its share alone would let a file without a parser grow inside it. Every emitted file outside the entry chunk of a 0.3.0 configuration is therefore gated on its own: a file that holds the ISO BMFF parser, the Matroska parser or an engine chunk may grow by the allowance of each one it holds, the same shares as the parser rows and the engine chunks, and every other file stays identical to the stage base.

groups.name: first MP4 under the 25.00 KB promise
groups.why: The 0.4.0 parser additions may spend 0.39 KB, then 0.01 KB, then 0.05 KB on the first MP4 path, and the three configurations that inline the worker stay at or below 24.95 KB, inside the 25.00 KB promise.

groups.name: first MP4 of the default configuration
groups.why: The same shares, under the 24.00 KB promise of the default configuration.

groups.name: first MP4 of the custom worker configurations
groups.why: The same shares, under the 0.3.0 budgets of the custom configurations.

groups.name: standalone ISO BMFF worker file
groups.why: The prebuilt ISO BMFF worker carries the same parser code as the first MP4 path.

groups.name: Matroska path
groups.why: The 0.4.0 parser additions may spend 0.20 KB, then 0.05 KB on the first MKV path, under the 0.3.0 budgets of these rows.

groups.name: first MP4 of the other configurations
groups.why: The same shares as the first MP4 rows above. These rows have no budget in the size matrix, so only their growth is gated.

groups.name: first MP4 of the other configurations with a budget
groups.why: The same shares as the first MP4 rows above, under the 0.3.0 budgets of these rows.

groups.name: first MKV of the other configurations
groups.why: The same shares as the Matroska path. These rows have no budget in the size matrix, so only their growth is gated.

groups.name: both parsers in one file
groups.why: The single standalone worker holds both parsers, so it, and the first file of the configuration that loads it, may grow by the ISO BMFF and the Matroska shares together.

groups.name: ISO BMFF parser chunk
groups.why: The parser chunk carries most of the first MP4 growth and stays under 13.00 KB.

groups.name: ISO BMFF parser chunk of the other configurations
groups.why: These rows measure the same parser code as the parser chunk above, so they get the same shares under the same 13.00 KB cap.

groups.name: Matroska parser chunk
groups.why: The Matroska parser in the own worker gets the shares of the Matroska path, under the 12.50 KB budget of the default and all configurations, which the other configurations measure the same parser code against.

groups.name: rate profile core
groups.why: No 0.4.0 stage changes the rate profile core, so it stays identical to 0.3.0, under the 2.00 KB budget of the default and all configurations, which the other configurations measure the same code against.

groups.name: ffprobe frame rate estimate
groups.why: No 0.4.0 stage changes the ffprobe frame rate estimate, so it stays identical to 0.3.0, under the 4.00 KB budget of the default and all configurations, which the other configurations measure the same code against.

groups.name: all own paths
groups.why: Every own path holds the ISO BMFF parser and the Matroska parser once, so it may grow by the ISO BMFF and the Matroska shares together, under the 0.3.0 budgets of these rows.

groups.name: all own paths of the other configurations
groups.why: The same shares as the all own paths above. These rows have no budget in the size matrix, so only their growth is gated.

groups.name: emitted lazy totals
groups.why: The emitted lazy total holds two copies of each parser, the one the worker loads and the main-thread copy, so it may grow by twice the ISO BMFF and the Matroska shares together, under the 0.3.0 budgets of these rows.

groups.name: emitted lazy totals with one engine worker
groups.why: The engine worker carries a third copy of each parser because it also serves own, so these rows may grow by three times the ISO BMFF and the Matroska shares together, under their 0.3.0 budgets.

groups.name: emitted lazy total with both engine workers
groups.why: Both engine workers carry a copy of each parser, so this row holds four copies and may grow by four times the ISO BMFF and the Matroska shares together, under its 0.3.0 budget. That budget of 367.00 KB is below the stage 5 allowance, 364,569 B as built in 0.3.0 plus 2,800 B. If the full design shares do not fit under it, stage 5 may re-set the lazy total budget of the all configuration, and this cap with it, to its measurement plus 1 percent, with a changelog note.

groups.name: engine chunks
groups.why: The library engine chunks share the result helpers and may grow by 0.03 KB at most, under their 0.3.0 budgets.

groups.name: main-thread engine chunks
groups.why: No 0.4.0 stage changes the rVFC engine or the shared engine chunk on the main thread, so they stay identical to 0.3.0, under their 0.3.0 budgets.

groups.name: critical path
groups.why: The package code in the entry chunk stays identical to 0.3.0 for the whole release, up to the content hashes of the chunk names it imports.

groups.name: critical path of the rule entries
groups.why: Byte-identical to 0.3.0 until the last 0.4.0 step, which adds the check rules and re-sets the preset budget.

groups.name: check chunk of the rule entries
groups.why: The check rules stay identical to 0.3.0 until the last 0.4.0 step, which adds the new rules, and then stay at or below 4.50 KB.

groups.name: preset data chunk
groups.why: No preset value changes in 0.4.0, so the preset data stays identical to 0.3.0 for the whole release.
